source.title: Slices of Brownian Sheet: New Results, and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let B = {B(s,t)}_{s,t≥0} be a two-parameter Brownian sheet in R^d, meaning a centered Gaussian process with covariance Cov(B_i(s,t), B_j(u,v)) = min(s,u) min(t,v) δ_{i,j}. For d ∈ {2,3}, fix any slice parameter s > 0 and consider the zero set of the slice, equivalently B^{-1}{0} ∩ ({s} × (0,∞)). Is it true that, outside one null event that works simultaneously for every s > 0, this set is finite for every s > 0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1. Suppose d ∈ { 2, 3}. Is it true that outside a single null set, B− 1{0} ∩ ({s} × (0, ∞ )) is a ﬁnite set for all s> 0?
Let B := {B(s,t )}s,t ≥ 0 denote a two-parameter Brownian sheet in Rd. That is, B is a centered Gaussian process with covariance matrix, Cov (Bi(s,t ), Bj(u,v )) = min(s,u ) ·min(t,v ) ·δi,j .

accepted.question_text: For a d-dimensional two-parameter Brownian sheet B and for each s ≥ 0, define Y_d(s) = {(t_1,t_2) ∈ R_+^2 : B(s,t_1) = B(s,t_2)}; this is the set of double points of the slice t ↦ B(s,t). If d ∈ {4,5}, is it true that outside one null event that works simultaneously for all s ≥ 0, the Hausdorff dimension of Y_d(s) is 0 for every s ≥ 0?
accepted.context_brief: Hausdorff dimension of slice double points

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2. Deﬁne, for all s ≥ 0, Yd(s) := {(t1,t 2) ∈ R2 + : B(s,t 1) = B(s,t 2)}. (8.2) Then is it the case that if d ∈ { 4, 5} then, outside a single null-set, dimH Yd(s) = 0 for all s ≥ 0?
Next, we consider the random set, Dd := {s ≥ 0 : B(s,t 1) = B(s,t 2) for some t2>t 1> 0}. (1.9) We can note that s ∈ Dd if and only if the slice of B along s has a double point.

accepted.question_text: For a d-dimensional two-parameter Brownian sheet B and Y_d(s) = {(t_1,t_2) ∈ R_+^2 : B(s,t_1) = B(s,t_2)}, if d ∈ {4,5}, does there exist an event of probability 1 on which Y_d(s) is finite for every s > 0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3. Let d ∈ { 4, 5}. Then is it true that outside a single null set, Yd(s) is a ﬁnite set for all s> 0?

accepted.question_text: Let B^{-1}{0} = {(s,t) : B(s,t)=0} be the zero set of a two-parameter Brownian sheet B in R^d. The paper shows that projection onto the s-axis preserves the Hausdorff dimension 2 - d/2 for the zero set in the relevant dimensions. Is there some random orthogonal projection of B^{-1}{0} whose image has Hausdorff dimension different from 2 - d/2?
accepted.context_brief: Random projections of the zero set

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4. Is there a (random) orthogonal projection such that the said projection of B− 1{0} has a diﬀerent Hausdorﬀ dimension than 2 − (d/ 2)?
Consequently, when d ∈ { 2, 3}, the [Hausdorﬀ] dimension of Zd is equal to 2 − (d/ 2). Oddly enough, this is precisely the dimension of B− 1{0} as well; see Rosen [29, 30].

accepted.question_text: Consider the hyperbolic stochastic PDE system (∂^2 u^i/∂t∂x) = b^i(u) + σ^i(u) · ˆB with reasonable boundary conditions, where σ: R^d → R^d is strongly elliptic, bounded, and C^∞. Do the same kinds of slice and exceptional-set results established earlier in the paper for the d-dimensional Brownian sheet also hold for solutions u of this multiplicative-noise system?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5. Supposeσ : Rd → Rd is a strongly elliptic, bounded, C∞ func- tion. Is it the case that the results of the previous sections apply to the solution of (∂ 2ui/∂t∂x ) = bi(u) +σi(u) · ˆB with reasonable boundary conditions?
Then, as long as b := (b1,...,b d) is bounded and Borel-measurable the law of the process u := (u1,...,u d) is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to
the law of the two-parameter, d-dimensional Brownian sheet B. See Proposition 1.6 of Nualart and Pardoux [24]. Therefore, the theorems of the preceding sections apply to the process u equally well.

accepted.question_text: Consider the linear parabolic SPDE system ∂u^i/∂t(t,x) = ∂^2 u^i/∂x^2(t,x) + ˆB_i(t,x) with reasonable boundary conditions. Is there a theory of the slices of the solution field u at fixed times t, analogous to the slice theory developed in this paper for Brownian sheets?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6. Consider the following system of linear parabolic SPDE: ∂ui/∂t (t,x ) = ∂ 2ui/∂x 2 (t,x ) + ˆBi(t,x ), (8.4) with reasonable boundary conditions. Is there an analysis of the “slices” of u along diﬀerent values of t that is analogous to the results of the present paper?

trace.notes: Resolved zbMATH record 5295972 to the exact-work arXiv PDF math/0510518. Mapped Section 8 (pages 33-35) as the primary open-problem region containing Open Problems 1-6.
Extracted Open Problem 1 from Section 8.1 (Slices and Zeros).
Extracted Open Problems 2 and 3 from Section 8.2 (Smallness of Double-Points for Slices).
Extracted Open Problem 4 from Section 8.3 (Marstrand's Theorem for Projections).
Extracted Open Problems 5 and 6 from Section 8.4 (Non-Linear SPDEs).
Expanded the slice-zero-set question by inlining the Brownian-sheet definition and interpreting B^{-1}{0} ∩ ({s} × (0,∞)) as the zero set within a fixed slice.
Rewrote Y_d(s) as the double-point set of a fixed slice and preserved the simultaneous almost-sure quantifier over all s ≥ 0.
Kept the finiteness question for Y_d(s) separate from the Hausdorff-dimension question because they are distinct open problems.
Made the projection question self-contained by identifying B^{-1}{0} as the Brownian-sheet zero set and carrying over the dimension value 2 - d/2 from the introduction.

Expanded 'results of the previous sections' into a self-contained reference to the paper's Brownian-sheet slice and exceptional-set results, supported by the preceding-page discussion of absolute continuity with Brownian sheet laws.
Restated the parabolic-SPDE question as a request for a Brownian-sheet-like slice theory for fixed-time slices of the solution field.
